# Independent audit: deterministic fractional gamma bound

**Result: PASS.** I independently read and checked the entire source
`candidate 93a759825a881af9`.
The theorem proves G_(k,p)>9/20 for every integer k>=1 and every
real p in [0,1]. I found no unresolved approximation or sampling step.

## Fourier and Taylor mechanism

For k>=3 the gamma density extended by zero has a continuous
integrable derivative and derivative transform -it(1-it)^(-k).
Its transform is absolutely integrable because its tail is
O(|t|^(1-k)). Direct integration gives

    integral_R |t|(1+t^2)^(-k/2)dt=2/(k-2).

Thus the displayed bound ||g_k'||_infinity<=1/[pi(k-2)] and its
weaker rational consequence <1/[3(k-2)] are correct. Convolution
with the negative exponential contracts the derivative supremum.
The source's survival-function Taylor remainder is global, so
integrating the unbounded centered noise p(E-1) is legitimate:
its first moment is zero and its second moment is p^2. This gives
the stated loss 1/[6(k-2)] without a local-tail assumption.

As an optional improvement, the characteristic function of
Gamma(k)-Exp itself has modulus (1+t^2)^(-(k+1)/2), which gives
the stronger bound ||f_k'||<=1/[pi(k-1)]. The source does not
need this improvement; its weaker constants already close all
ranges.

## Lipschitz interpolation

The differentiated probability and the exponential integration by
parts have the correct signs. The latter yields exactly

    G'_(k,p)=-p f'_(W_k+p Gamma(2))(k+p-1).

Size bias is applied to the exponential of mean one before scaling
by p, so no additional p factor or reciprocal is missing. The
Lipschitz interpretation at k=1 is valid: the density is globally
Lipschitz, its exceptional derivative point has zero probability
when p>0, and bounded convergence handles p=0. The k=2 derivative
bound 1/4 is also exact as an upper bound. Hence the mesh radius
1/64 and all three interpolation errors, 1/128, 1/256, and 1/192,
are justified on the full closed interval.

## Integer endpoint and infinite-k estimates

I checked the gamma-tail formula, the centered gamma density
pairing, and the falling-factorial bound on its subtracted term.
The logarithm integral has the correct inequality direction:
concavity gives log(m!)>=integral_(1/2)^(m+1/2)log x, and the
following lower bound uses log(1+x)>=x/(1+x). It yields exactly
q_m<=1/sqrt(2em)<sqrt(3/(16m)). Both errors used at k>=83 are
decreasing. The displayed positive rational square difference
certifies the cutoff without taking a square root of an unknown
sign.

The bound e<87/32 is correct: the series through degree five is
163/60, and its tail is at most 7/4320, summing to
87/32-1/2160. The resulting rational gamma lower bound has the
correct direction because its coefficients are positive.

## Signed exponential enclosures: independent algebra check

Besides checking the source's integration-by-parts recurrence, I
independently obtained the two exponential coefficients by partial
fractions of the Laplace transform of Gamma(k)+p Exp. For 0<p<1,
set

    c_j=(-p)^(k-j)/(1-p)^(k-j+1),       1<=j<=k,
    c_* =(-p)^k/(1-p)^k.

Its density is the signed mixture of Gamma(j) densities with
coefficients c_j and the mean-p exponential density with
coefficient c_*. Therefore, at s=k-1+p,

    G_(k,p)=e^(-s) sum_(j=1)^k c_j Q_j(s)
                    +e^(-s/p) c_* p/(1+p).

This is the same pair of coefficients A,B as in the source.
An independent rational check compared these expressions with
the source's recurrence at all 341 interior mesh points, giving
**682 exact coefficient identities**. Thus the enclosure does
not rest on an unchecked shared sign convention in the primitive.

The degree-32 upper and degree-33 lower alternating Taylor sums
have the claimed direction for 0<=r<=1. Grouping adjacent terms
gives positivity of the lower sum, including r=1. Factoring a
general rational x into its integer and fractional parts therefore
preserves interval order. Reversing interval endpoints for each
negative coefficient A or B correctly encloses every cancellation.

## Executed certificate and coverage

I reran
`supporting computation verify_deterministic_fractional_gamma_uniform_bound_coherent.py`.
It passed all 363 rational mesh intervals, all 71 finite gamma
bounds, all seven extra tail entries, and every displayed cutoff
and interpolation gap. In particular its current certificate
includes k=1 and k=2, so no endpoint-minimum theorem is an implicit
dependency.

The ranges k<=11, 12<=k<=82, and k>=83 exhaust every positive
integer k. The proved Lipschitz bounds exhaust every real p between
the mesh points. Both endpoints p=0,1 are evaluated by their exact
gamma formulas and are also limits of the underlying probabilities.
Thus no fixed-dimensional computational conjecture remains in
this theorem.

This audit does not claim OC or the separate coefficient-stratum
escape reduction. The latter requires its own compactness and
normal-limit proof; the audited result supplies its deterministic
negative scalar input.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
